text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- According to a group of Moslem returnees who entered the village of Gajevi in Bosnia's Serb republic, there are no conditions for normal life in the village and help from local officials will be necessary.
- President of opposition Social Democratic Party (SDP), Nijaz Durakovic, proposes the Moslem-Croat Federation Forum to meet and resolve all federal problems.
- Bosnian Council of Ministers met again on Thursday but has yet not established its working procedure since it could not agree on voting rights of deputy ministers.
- Experts from Bosnia and Croatia should soon begin to mark boundary lines at the border crossings between the two countries, Bosnian Ambassador to Croatia Kasim Trnka says.

- Private company Lijanovic from Croat controlled part of Bosnia denies that the Moslem-Croat Federation government's deputy prime minister Drago Bilandzija helped them avoid paying taxes for goods they have imported.

- Spanish troops of NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) and U.N. police monitors have confiscated illegal weapons from a police station in Croat-controlled part of divided Bosnian town of Mostar, NATO says.
